organization.summary: Described on its GitHub organization as a digital asset investment firm and open-source Ethereum security contributor, created 2026-01-01. Its website lists Luxembourg. The proposal names no individual team members.

claims.claim: The safe-lockdown-guard repository is public and MIT licensed, with the tag v1.0.0-audit-candidate.3.
claims.method: GitHub API: MIT, created 2026-08-26, last push 2026-11-12, tags v1.0.0-audit-candidate.3 and v1.0.0-audit-nethermind.

claims.claim: The audit brief records 1,118 non-comment source lines, 483 passing tests and 15 stateful invariant properties.
claims.method: The brief states 1118 nSLOC across 10 files, 483 tests passed, and 15 Echidna stateful invariants passing. The tests were not rerun.

claims.claim: The candidate is not yet externally audited.
claims.method: The README on HEAD (commit of 2026-11-12) says 'Audited by Nethermind Security (NM-1060)' and that the report will be published in the repository. The Runtime Guard page repeats it with 'report publication pending'. The proposal text may describe an earlier state; the proposal date was not compared with the README commit. A tag v1.0.0-audit-nethermind exists, dated 2026-11-01.

claims.claim: A public Nethermind audit report exists.
claims.method: The repository listing was searched for 1060, lockdown and runtime and returned no match. The Runtime-Capital README says the report will be published.

claims.claim: The project was awarded a subsidy of up to $6,500 through the Ethereum Security Subsidy Program.
claims.method: The page describes the program (up to 30% off audits, committee of Ethereum Foundation, Chainlink Labs and Nethermind Security with Areta). It does not name Runtime Capital or an award.

claims.claim: The guard has been deployed on Ethereum mainnet and used on an operational Safe.
claims.method: The README states 'Ethereum mainnet deployment in progress'. No deployment address is named in the proposal, so no onchain lookup was made.
